title: Drop and Cover
premise: Silas Pemberton, a veteran crash investigator, has spent six years chasing the truth about Flight 4471, which killed her husband and daughter in row twelve — and which three governments insist never existed. When a live flight's records evaporate mid-air and its passengers begin dying in 'accidents,' Silas realizes the same black-box program that erased her family's flight is still running. Forced to ally with a disgraced air marshal and a teenage survivor who shouldn't be alive, she smuggles recovered flight data across three borders while an assassin closes in. In the end, Silas broadcasts the evidence at the cost of nearly her own life, chooses her makeshift family over her obsession, and finally unpacks the go-bag.
about_author: Mara Blackwood is a former aviation insurance analyst who spent a decade reading accident reports before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside systems designed to forget them.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. On the sixth anniversary of the crash, Silas rehearses her polished lie at a memorial hearing, go-bag by the door. A junior colleague notices the flight number isn't in any database. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into routine; the reader learns what she lost and how tightly she holds it together.

chapters.title: The Vanishing
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Mid-shift, every record of airborne Flight 882 — manifests, radar logs, passenger lists — deletes itself in real time. Silas screenshots everything before the wipe completes. Beat: dread and adrenaline as her private conspiracy becomes an active crime happening in front of her.

chapters.title: Ninety-Six Souls
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Daniel Okafor, an air marshal grounded after reporting tampered maintenance logs. The plane lands; ninety-six passengers disembark into buses that never arrive. Beat: mounting horror as the 'erased' become disposable people.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Wasn't Listed
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Among the survivors she finds Wren, sixteen, whose name appears on no manifest but who remembers everything, including a man in the cockpit doorway. Beat: reluctant connection — Silas recognizes her own daughter's stubbornness and can't walk away.

chapters.title: Go-Bag
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. An official 'wellness check' turns into surveillance; Silas grabs the bag she's packed for six years and runs with Wren. Beat: the lie collapses; survival mode activates, and found family begins forming under pressure.

chapters.title: The Cleaner
chapters.summary: Assassin Vesper Kade's POV, cold and procedural. She erases two witnesses in Reykjavik and receives Silas's file — including the detail that Silas was on the original waitlist for Flight 4471. Beat: chilling intimacy of being hunted by someone who knows your grief.

chapters.title: Black Box
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. He recovers a damaged recorder from the impounded aircraft and decodes a fragment: a mid-flight command signature from a ground station that officially doesn't exist. Beat: hope with teeth — proof exists, but holding it is a death sentence.

chapters.title: Three Governments
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A sympathetic intelligence contact offers asylum for the data, then Silas overhears him selling it upward. She realizes all three governments want the fragment buried, not exposed. Beat: betrayal; trust becomes a currency she can no longer spend freely.

chapters.title: Wren's Memory
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Under Silas's careful questioning, Wren recalls the cockpit visitor's badge and a phrase: 'Protocol Drop and Cover.' Beat: tenderness and trauma intertwined; Wren stops being cargo and becomes the investigation's heart.

chapters.title: Border Crossing
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A harrowing ferry crossing with the data hidden in Wren's jacket; border drones sweep the deck. Silas teaches Wren her old investigator tricks. Beat: mentorship blooming into motherhood neither will name yet.

chapters.title: Kade Closes
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She corners Daniel in a safehouse; he escapes wounded but leaves the decoy drive behind. Vesper reports success — then doubts it. Beat: first hairline crack in the assassin's certainty, humanizing the hunter.

chapters.title: The Program
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV, recovering in hiding. Decoded fragments reveal 'Drop and Cover': a kill-switch protocol that can erase any aircraft's existence, sold to governments as deniable disaster management. Flight 4471 was its first test. Beat: righteous fury; Silas's conspiracy theory becomes documented fact.

chapters.title: What Silas Buried
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Flashback chapter: Silas gave up her seat on 4471 after a fight with her husband; survivor's guilt built both her career and her lie. Beat: devastating vulnerability — the go-bag wasn't readiness, it was punishment.

chapters.title: Safehouse
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The trio shelters in Daniel's childhood home; Wren cooks, they argue about music, and for one evening they're almost a family. Beat: warmth as counterweight — showing exactly what they stand to lose.

chapters.title: The Waitlist
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Vesper ambushes them, but hesitates when Silas names Flight 4471 aloud — Vesper's own brother died on a 'vanished' charter years ago. Standoff ends unresolved. Beat: enemy revealed as fellow orphan of the program; moral lines blur.

chapters.title: Broadcast Tower
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Plan formed: transmit the full decoded archive through an independent satellite uplink during a global aviation summit, when the world is watching. Beat: ticking clock established; hope now has a deadline.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Government forces seize their route; Daniel is captured buying time. Silas must choose between rescuing him and making the window. Beat: agonizing sacrifice — she sends Wren ahead alone and goes back for Daniel.

chapters.title: Drop and Cover
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Ordered to execute Daniel, Vesper instead gives him the summit's security rotation — her defection sealed by her brother's name. Beat: the assassin chooses memory over mission; the theme of belonging overtakes even her.

chapters.title: Uplink
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Climax. On the summit floor, under fire, Silas physically holds the transmitter open while the archive streams worldwide — vanished flights, falsified crashes, row twelve among them. She takes a bullet. Beat: catharsis through exposure; truth finally louder than the lie.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Hospitals, hearings, headlines. The program's architects fall; some records return; most don't. Wren refuses to be listed as an orphan, listing Silas and Daniel as guardians instead. Beat: grief transmuted into chosen family, formalized on paper.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, recovering. She testifies publicly, saying her family's names into the record for the first time without flinching. Vesper watches from the gallery, free on cooperation terms. Beat: reckoning and release; the polished lie finally retired.

chapters.title: Unpacked
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Months later, in a small house near the coast, Silas empties the go-bag item by item — flashlight, cash, the old boarding pass — and packs a suitcase instead, for a trip the three of them take together. Beat: quiet resolution; belonging replaces escape, and the story lands softly where it began.
